title: Central Bank of Kenya Guidance Note on Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP), November 2016
first_as_of_note: The Guidance Note carries an issue month (November 2016) and no commencement date; the first annual report is taken to be the one as at 31 December 2016 (¶5(b)).

documents.title: Guidance Note on Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP)

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.guidance: Summary of the capital planning process, risk exposure and total internal capital (Guidance Note ¶1(a), ¶5(a), ¶5(c)).

requirements.text: Show that total capital is adequate and consistent with the strategy, business plan, risk profile and operating environment on a going-concern basis.
Give the CBK what it needs for a complete, documented assessment of the capital planning process, overall risk exposure and total internal capital.
From the capital reported at the previous year-end, set out the strategy for taking on risk and meeting the related capital needs through the end of the current year.

sections.title: Design, Approval, Review, and Use of ICAAP
sections.guidance: How the ICAAP is designed, approved, reviewed, controlled and used (¶2, ¶3, ¶4(i)(c), ¶4(v), ¶4(vi); Annex B §2(a)–(b)).

requirements.text: Keep the ICAAP formalised and documented.
Subject the ICAAP to internal review and approval by the Board and management.
Protect the integrity of the process through internal controls, independent reviews and audits.
Present the ICAAP simply and intuitively.
Show that methods, stress tests, correlation treatment, control organisation and reporting scope are proportionate to the size, nature and complexity of the business.
Have the Board review and approve the ICAAP policies at least every {param:icaap_review_max_months} months or when specific events prompt it, keeping them compliant with supervisory requirements.
Describe the process for preparing and updating the ICAAP.
Describe the process for reviewing the ICAAP.
Monitor and report material risks and trends, the sensitivity of key assumptions, capital sufficiency against goals and future capital needs, adjusting the ICAAP as needed.
Ensure strict segregation of duties, clear authority and a transparent, documented decision-making process.
Have internal audit review ICAAP application and adherence to controls, report shortcomings to the Board and senior management, and follow up their resolution.
Carry out independent reviews and audits at least as often as the governed interval of {param:icaap_independent_review_max_months} months.
Transmit the report formally to the CBK.

sections.title: Structure and Operations
sections.guidance: Group structure and where risks sit across operating units and legal entities (¶4(ii)(f); Annex B §3(b)).

requirements.text: In a banking group, implement the ICAAP on a consolidated basis, showing consolidated capital supports parent and subsidiary activities and absorbs their potential losses.
Map risks to the bank's operating units and, for a group, its legal entities.

sections.title: Governance Structure
sections.guidance: Board and senior management oversight of capital (¶4(i); Annex B §2(c)–(f)).

requirements.text: Show the Board and senior management ensure capital supports the bank's risks, allowing it to operate as a going concern and to grow.
Establish capital planning and management policies in line with the CBK corporate governance guideline.
State the definition of capital used in the ICAAP clearly, apply it consistently and align it with the CBK capital adequacy guideline.
Define the roles and functions of the Board and senior management bodies in the ICAAP.
Define the roles and functions of corporate functions in the ICAAP, such as internal audit, compliance, planning and risk management.
Describe the organisational and contractual safeguards over any outsourced element of the ICAAP.
Indicate the internal regulations relevant to the ICAAP.

sections.title: Summary of business plan and strategy
sections.guidance: Business plan, budgets and how capital goals relate to strategy (¶2(f), ¶4(ii)(c); Annex B §1(a)).

requirements.text: Describe the business plan and annual budgets, the schedule for reviewing them and the extraordinary events that would trigger a review.
Relate the capital adequacy goals to risks, strategic focus and the business plan.

sections.title: Risk Appetite Statement
sections.guidance: The bank's risk appetite statement (Annex B §7(f)); the Guidance Note gives no further detail.

requirements.text: Set out the risk appetite statement.

sections.title: Risk Assessment and Capital Adequacy
sections.guidance: Identification and measurement of material risks, internal capital by risk, allocation and reconciliation (¶2(b)–(e), ¶4(ii)(b), ¶4(iii); Annex A; Annex B §3–§5).

requirements.text: Identify and measure the risks of the business comprehensively and assess the capital needed to support them.
Show interactions between risks under normal and stressed conditions, including external risks from the regulatory, economic and business environment.
Keep comprehensive, continually reviewed policies to identify, measure, monitor, control and report risks, considering at least the risks in Annex A.
Use measurement systems rigorous enough to capture the nature and size of each risk and differentiate exposures consistently.
Ensure controls make risk identification objective and consistent and that all material on- and off-balance-sheet risks are addressed.
Assess hard-to-quantify risks qualitatively with management judgement, recognising the biases and limits of that approach so the impact is not understated.
Maintain the infrastructure and management information systems needed for firm-wide risk oversight.
Where risk mitigation is used, understand the risk mitigated and the effect of the mitigation, with policies to control the risks of those techniques.
Hold capital for the measured risks plus an additional amount for the uncertainties the ICAAP identifies.
Map the bank's position against Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 risks.
For every measurable risk category, describe the main risk control and mitigation instruments.
Describe the systems for controlling and mitigating non-measurable risks.
Quantify internal capital for each risk and in total.
Describe any method for allocating internal capital to operating units or legal entities.
Reconcile total internal capital with regulatory requirements.
List and define the capital components covering internal capital.
State the supervisory eligibility of each component and explain the inclusion of any ineligible component.
Estimate the cost of using capital sources beyond those already used.

sections.title: Methodology and Assumptions
sections.guidance: Measurement methods, their validation, limitations and key assumptions (¶2(h), ¶4(iii)(d)–(e),(h); Annex B §3(c)).

requirements.text: Validate regularly the methodology, data and systems used to model the probability and consequences of individual risks and their aggregation.
Support the accuracy and appropriateness of the measurement techniques with detailed analyses.
Identify and understand the limitations of the quantification and measurement methods.
Validate third-party inputs and tools, such as ratings, risk measures and models, initially and on an ongoing basis.
Describe the techniques used for risk measurement, internal capital determination and stress testing.

sections.title: Stress Testing
sections.guidance: Forward-looking stress testing of capital adequacy (¶4(iv)).

requirements.text: Include forward-looking stress test results over at least {param:icaap_stress_horizon_years_min} years, say whether the longer horizon the Guidance Note prefers was used, and base them on plausible adverse circumstances.
Use sensitivity and scenario analysis to find events or market changes that could seriously affect capital and operations.
Obtain a forward-looking view of capital adequacy from stress tests and scenario analysis.
Make stress testing part of governance and culture, with results that drive decisions of the Board and senior management, who take part in the programme.
Run a programme that supports risk identification and control, complements other tools and improves capital and liquidity management and communication.
Govern the programme with written policies and procedures and document its operation.
Apply the CBK prudential guideline on stress testing.

sections.title: Capital Planning
sections.guidance: The capital plan, targets, horizons and sources of capital (¶2(b), ¶4(i)(d)–(e), ¶4(ii)(a),(d),(e); Annex B §1(b)–(c)).

requirements.text: Show current and prospective capital for all material risks over a forecast period of at least {param:icaap_capital_planning_horizon_years_min} years, and say whether the longer horizon the Guidance Note prefers was used.
Maintain a capital plan setting out current and future capital needs, expected capital expenditure, the desired capital level, external sources and required actions.
Set guiding principles for choosing and prioritising capital actions under different scenarios, weighing value added, costs, benefits and market conditions.
Include capital targets and horizons, the planning process and responsibilities, the intent to meet regulatory requirements and a contingency plan for divergences.
Set an internal strategy for maintaining capital that reflects growth expectations, future sources and uses of funds and dividend policy.
Show how other considerations, such as external rating goals and market image, influenced the amount of capital held.
Reconcile the time horizon of the business plan with that of the capital plan.
Describe the sources of Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital.

sections.title: Use of Internal Models for Capital Assessment
sections.guidance: Internal models used for capital assessment (Annex B §7(k); ¶2(h)).

requirements.text: Where internal models are used for capital assessment, describe them and show their methodology, data and systems are validated regularly.
Identify the areas of the ICAAP process that could be improved.
Plan the capital or organisational actions that follow.

risk_categories.title: Interest rate risk in the banking book
Liquidity risks (liquidity profile and market liquidity)
Compliance with minimum standards and disclosure requirements
Other material risks (Annex A lists some of the risks to consider)

attachments.title: Evidence of Board and management approval of the ICAAP
Independent review or internal audit report on the ICAAP
Source evidence for a manually entered table

stages.title: Board Risk Committee challenge and approval
Board approval (signature on the frozen report)

material_change_triggers.label: Significant acquisition opportunity or similar specific event

materiality_matrix.note: The CBK Guidance Note prescribes no scoring matrix. This is the platform starting point, adjusted by the bank in P2.

notes.text: The Guidance Note sets high-level minimum requirements rather than prescribed methods; banks design the ICAAP to their own needs.
The submission date is a fixed calendar day after a 31 December position; the governed months-after-year-end value reproduces it with month-end clamping.
The CBK uses the results to set the capital adequacy level it requires of the bank and may require improvements to capital and risk processes.
No Board resolution attachment is prescribed; approval evidence is optional.
The Guidance Note contains no requirement to publish ICAAP results, so this framework declares no disclosure specification.
No CBK ICAAP return is registered yet; cycles support drafting, readiness and draft exports, and freeze refuses until a return family for this regulator exists.

The Guidance Note states a minimum capital and stress horizon and a longer horizon it prefers. Only the minimum is a governed parameter today; the preferred horizon is asked for in words until a code is seeded for it, and ships as a new framework version when it is.
